name: Prosper of Aquitaine
knownFor: A writer from Gaul who took Augustine of Hippo's side on grace against the monks of Marseilles, wrote against John Cassian, and kept a chronicle of his own times.
dates: Wrote to Augustine shortly before Augustine's death; Edgar Gibson dates the letter to 429. His chronicle runs, as Gennadius of Marseilles read it, to the Vandal capture of Rome; Theodor Mommsen, its editor, reasons from it that he lived at least to 455. No ancient source used here gives his birth or death. The years 403 to 463 are an editor's note in E. C. Richardson's translation of Gennadius

keyWorks.title: Letter to Augustine
keyWorks.about: reports that many servants of Christ at Marseilles thought Augustine's teaching on God's calling of the chosen went against the Fathers; held in Latin among Augustine's letters

keyWorks.title: Chronicle (Epitoma Chronicon)
keyWorks.about: a chronicle from the creation to his own day; its entries give the mission of Germanus of Auxerre to Britain, Palladius sent to the Irish, and the death of Augustine of Hippo

keyWorks.title: Book against Cassian
keyWorks.about: an unsigned book against works of John Cassian that Gennadius of Marseilles thought was Prosper's; not held

traces: His chronicle is the source the Library holds for Pope Celestine sending Germanus, bishop of Auxerre, to Britain, and for Palladius sent as first bishop to the Irish who believed in Christ.
Gennadius of Marseilles reports that letters of Leo of Rome against Eutyches were thought to have been dictated by him.
remembered: Gennadius of Marseilles: "a man scholastic in style and vigorous in statement".
Photius, in his Library, calls him "truly a man of God".
Edgar Gibson, translator of John Cassian, on his book against Cassian: "a treatise of considerable power and force, although not scrupulously fair".

uncertain: Whether he was a layman is disputed. Edgar Gibson calls him "also a layman", and Garnier, editor of Marius Mercator, counts him among laymen. Theodor Mommsen thinks him a cleric when he wrote to Augustine, since he calls the deacon Leontius his brother. Mommsen also rejects the view that he was a bishop.
That the unsigned book against Cassian is Prosper's is the judgment of Gennadius of Marseilles, who sided with Cassian. The book is not held.

Gennadius says letters of Leo against Eutyches "are also thought" to have been dictated by him; some manuscripts read "said", as Richardson's note gives it. Mommsen says medieval writers made him a notary of the Roman church, and that Gennadius's account does not show he even left Gaul.
Gibson dates the letter to Augustine to 429 because it names Hilary as newly bishop of Arles. The appeal to Pope Celestine with a layman named Hilary is Gibson's account.

No ancient source used here gives his birth, death or city. Gennadius gives his region, Aquitaine. The years 403 to 463 are Richardson's note to Gennadius and a note in J. H. Freese's translation of Photius; Mommsen says only that he lived at least to 455.
The chronicle's years are Mommsen's: Prosper dates by consuls.
